title: Work, Energy & Power
summary: Work is $W=Fd\cos\theta$; it changes kinetic energy ($W_{net}=\Delta KE$). Gravitational and elastic potential energy store work, and mechanical energy is conserved without friction. Power is the rate of doing work, $P=W/t=Fv$.

work.plain: Energy transferred by a force over distance.

work-energy theorem.plain: Net work equals change in KE.

efficiency.in_class: Always less than 100% in real machines.

concept_sections.heading: Work
concept_sections.explanation: Work is force times displacement in the force's direction: $W=Fd\cos\theta$. A perpendicular force does no work; friction does negative work.

concept_sections.heading: Kinetic energy and the work–energy theorem
concept_sections.explanation: A moving mass has $KE=\tfrac12mv^2$, and the net work done on it equals the change in that energy: $W_{net}=\Delta KE$.

figure.caption: Kinetic energy and the work–energy theorem

concept_sections.heading: Potential energy
concept_sections.explanation: Gravitational PE is $U=mgh$; elastic PE is $\tfrac12kx^2$. These store the work done against gravity or in a spring.

concept_sections.heading: Conservation of energy
concept_sections.explanation: Without friction, mechanical energy $KE+U$ is conserved; set the total at two points equal to find a speed or height. Friction converts some to heat.
math_steps: With friction, subtract the heat lost.

concept_sections.heading: Power
concept_sections.explanation: Power measures how fast work is done: $P=W/t$, or $P=Fv$ for a steady force at speed $v$. Its unit is the watt.
math_steps: Divide work by time, or use $Fv$.

real_world_examples.title: Climbing stairs
real_world_examples.scenario: You raise your body up several floors.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Work $mgh$ is done against gravity; power depends on how fast you climb.

real_world_examples.title: A roller coaster drop
real_world_examples.scenario: A car speeds up going downhill.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Potential energy converts to kinetic — conservation of energy without much friction.

real_world_examples.title: An electric motor's rating
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: $P=Fv$ tells the force it can sustain at a given speed.
